feed.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network

entry.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
entry.summary:
Significant progress has been made on the gossip-observer infrastructure since February. The system has amassed a substantial dataset, now publicly available on Zenodo at [https://zenodo.org/records/23111326](https://zenodo.org/records/23111326), with monthly updates planned. For those requiring more frequent data, daily updates are maintained in a private S3 bucket, accessible by direct message or through a Github issue on the observer repository.
A dedicated site for visualizing and analyzing metrics derived from this data has also been established at [https://gossip-observer.jharveyb.xyz/](https://gossip-observer.jharveyb.xyz/). This platform not only showcases many previously discussed metrics but also introduces new insights obtained from snapshots of the infrastructure nodes’ gossip graphs. Users are encouraged to propose additional metrics by opening issues on Github.
Attention has shifted toward leveraging Minisketch technology for a potential overhaul of the gossip protocol. An evolving draft extension BOLT, reflecting ongoing research and feedback, is available at [this Github link](https://github.com/jharveyb/bolts/blob/dd9f97a87518d62b82460b2b6e4e274663ec126a/bolt-gossip-minisketch.md). Since the Lightning Summit in May 2026, several pertinent observations have emerged. Firstly, both sketch extension and bisection techniques currently appear unjustified given their implementation complexity. Decoding performance targets have become clearer; specifically, the aim is to keep worst-case decode times to approximately 100 milliseconds on a Raspberry Pi 5 equipped with hardware acceleration. Additionally, the architecture of the message flow must be meticulously crafted to prevent exploitation by malicious peers who might otherwise trigger excessive CPU consumption.
A newly identified challenge accompanying set reconciliation within the gossip network has come to light, termed *message equivocation*. A detailed, preliminary definition is forthcoming in subsequent communications.
